key_insight: A concise, practical overview showing how explainable AI techniques can be adapted to and evaluated for protein language models, bridging black‑box sequence models with biologically meaningful interpretations.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of systematic guidance and evaluation for interpreting protein language models, clarifying which XAI methods reveal sequence–structure–function relationships and what their limitations are.
method: Survey and taxonomy of XAI techniques applied to protein LMs (e.g., attention analysis, probing classifiers, attribution/saliency methods, concept activation).
Mapping model-derived signals to biological entities (amino-acid importance, structural motifs, functional sites) and discussing experimental/benchmark evaluation strategies.
Practical recommendations and best practices for choosing, validating and reporting interpretability methods in protein ML workflows.
impact: Equips AI/ML and computational biology practitioners with a principled toolkit to interpret protein language models, improving model trust, hypothesis generation, and downstream experimental prioritization.
visual_elements: Taxonomy diagram grouping interpretability methods (attention, probing, attribution, concept-based) with short pros/cons labels.
Pipeline graphic showing steps: protein sequence → language model → interpretability method → mapping to structure/function → validation.
Example heatmap/sequence logo visualizing attribution scores over a protein sequence and mapped onto a 3D structure snapshot.
Benchmark bar chart comparing evaluation criteria (faithfulness, stability, biological relevance) across common XAI methods.
paper_title: Towards the explainability of protein language models
